title: Borel subgroup schemes
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field] [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G,B$ be $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme]. A morphism $i:B\to G$ exhibits a Borel subgroup if it is a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], $B$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] and solvable in the scheme-theoretic derived-series sense [def-sfb-semisimple-group-scheme], and it is maximal with these properties: for every smooth connected solvable closed subgroup $j:D\to G$, if there is $f:B\to D$ with $j\circ f=i$, then there is $r:D\to B$ with $i\circ r=j$. For the affine finite-type smooth connected groups of the item, this is precisely a maximal smooth connected solvable subgroup.
